Google review of Vons (5 out of 5, by Ta Conner, 2 months ago): Daniel and Ganae at Vons on Wilshire went ABOVE AND BEYOND for me!

I had less than 24 hours to get a custom cake with a photo on it and at least 6 different bakeries told me it was IMPOSSIBLE bc it required at least 48 hours notice. For some reason, I called Vons on Wilshire back for the second try and, this time, Daniel answered the phone. I explained to him that i DESPERATELY needed the cake for a very special occasion (a co-worker who is like a daughter was turning 22 and I overheard her trying to buy her own cake!). He told me not to worry, that he could get it done by 9AM the next morning! He walked me thru the ENTIRE process OVER THE PHONE (everyone else demanded i place the order thru the app, which made the turnaround time IMPOSSIBLE). He recommended a good size and shape for the cake and EVERYTHING down to the icing trim. I was literally in shock! He even gave me his cell # so I could reach out for updates. Who does that?!??!

Here's where I had to trust the process...He was leaving in 30 minutes (3:30 pm), the decorator wasnt there, but he assured me he would leave the precise details INCLUDING the urgent turnaround time for the decorator who would be in the following morning at 4 AM (and he would arrive at 7 AM). Mind u, I need this cake by 9!. So now im supposed to trust that another person is going ti get in board to make this whole thing happen???!?! YES!

Next morning, rolled at the bed ASAP and called VONS. The cake was already done and all Ganae had to do was write Happy Birthday on the side!!!!

When I arrived to pick up the cake, I almost fainted from how amazingly beautiful the cake was! Better than I expected! I hugged Daniel and Ganae so tight and couldn't stop thanking them enough. This was more than just getting a cake done, i really wanted to bless a young lady with a surprise for her birthday. And not just any surprise. She was literally trying to order her own cake! And when the other coworkers and I came out with the cake, the look in her eyes and the smile on her face was PRICELESS.

GOD BLESS DANIEL AND GANAE for their professionalism and expertise, but most of all, their EXTRA EFFORTS AND KINDNESS!

Google review of The Cheesecake Factory (5 out of 5, by Mariana Moraes, 4 months ago): I’ve been going to The Cheesecake Factory for years, even before I moved to the United States. It’s actually one of the places I always take friends and family when they come visit because I feel like it gives such a fun “American dining experience.” Their menu is huge, with so many options for every taste, which makes it perfect for groups.

This time, we went to celebrate my husband’s birthday, and as always, the food was delicious. We ordered from the SkinnyLicious menu because we wanted lighter options, and I honestly love that they offer meals that are less caloric without sacrificing flavor. Everything I’ve had there over the years has always been consistently tasty.

I also really love the atmosphere. Every location has the same signature look and feel, and I think the restaurants are beautifully decorated, warm colors, elegant details, and a very welcoming environment. It feels polished and comforting at the same time.

And of course, the cheesecakes are amazing. I’ve tried many flavors over the years, and not a single one disappointed me. They truly live up to the hype.

The only reason I’m giving 4 stars instead of 5 for service is because of a small disappointment during this visit. Since it was my husband’s birthday, we thought he would receive a complimentary cheesecake slice, which had always been part of our past experiences there. Our waiter wasn’t very clear that this had changed, and in the end, we were charged for it. Later, I found out that now you need to be part of the Rewards program to receive the birthday cheesecake. If I had known, I definitely would have signed up beforehand to continue the tradition.

Even with that, we still had a great experience overall, and it continues to be one of my favorite classic American restaurants

Google review of The Cheesecake Factory (5 out of 5, by Tommy Ramsey, 7 months ago): Santa Monica Nights, Cold Air, Warm Moments

We kicked off an early Saint Patrick’s Day this past weekend out in Santa Monica, and I’m not going to lie, it was one of those nights you just sit back and appreciate.
The place was packed. Energy everywhere. People out celebrating, music in the air, just a good vibe all around. It felt like the whole city showed up.
Now the only thing that tried to ruin it was that cold fog rolling in off the water. It hit hard. One minute you’re good, next minute you’re freezing. That ocean air doesn’t play around.

But even that couldn’t touch the night we were having.

My wife and I ended up at The Cheesecake Factory, and that’s where everything just settled in right. We were told it would be about a 40 minute wait for a table, but honestly, we didn’t even care. We grabbed seats at the bar instead.

Best decision we could have made.

We were already in celebration mode, so sitting at the bar just fit the moment. Drinks flowing, appetizers coming out, no rush, no pressure. Just us enjoying the night.

And the food hit. Exactly how it’s supposed to.

The Cheesecake Factory doesn’t miss when it comes to variety and consistency. The appetizers came out hot, flavorful, and right on time. No drop in quality, even with how packed it was. That says a lot.
What stood out even more was how welcoming everything felt. Even though we switched things up and stayed at the bar, there was no attitude, no disconnect. We were taken care of the whole time.
By the time our table was ready, we were already done eating. And you know what? That was perfectly fine. We didn’t need it. We already had the experience.

But let’s be real.

The best part of the night had nothing to do with the crowd, the drinks, or even the food.

It was being there with my wife.

Talking, laughing, just locked into each other with everything else going on around us. She makes everything better. Every place feels different when she’s there. More real. More complete.
That’s what I’ll remember.
Not the wait. Not the fog.
Just us.
And nights like that, you don’t take for granted.

Google review of Benihana - Santa Monica (2 out of 5, by javier hierro, 4 months ago): Warning: do not come to this place.

First of all, we had a reservation for 8:00 PM. As soon as we arrived and walked through the door, the reception area was completely packed with people. There was barely any room to stand. We were told that, regardless of having a reservation, we would need to wait around 20–30 minutes because of how crowded it was. In the end, we were seated at a table all the way at the back at 8:59 PM — almost one full hour after our reservation time.

At least the staff working at the small bar upstairs, where guests are asked to wait, were friendly. There was only one girl working alone behind a bar full of people. This is not really the employees' fault, but rather a consequence of how the restaurant is managed. It was obvious that the staff were overwhelmed and unable to keep up with demand. There are around 15 teppanyaki stations and only 4 chefs. Since each station serves two tables, that's effectively 30 tables, with each chef handling two stations at the same time.

Once seated, our order was not taken until 9:20 PM. Again, this was not the fault of the staff, who were clearly overworked and understaffed. We then had to wait another 20 minutes for the first appetizers, which were just a simple soup and salad that should not take long to prepare. In fact, I did not eat any cooked food until 10:15 PM.

One positive aspect is that the chefs are not restricted to a fixed, scripted performance. They have quite a lot of personality and interact with guests, make jokes, and create their own atmosphere, which was enjoyable.

The restaurant itself was extremely dirty. The floors were covered with paper scraps and other trash, there were pieces of food everywhere, the railings felt sticky, and even the restroom was somewhat dirty.

In the end, we were able to speak with the manager about the situation. He acknowledged the issues and gave us a discount on the bill, which allowed us to leave the tip that the waitstaff genuinely deserved. Throughout the evening, the servers remained professional, friendly, and did the best they could under very difficult circumstances.

Overall, the experience was a little disappointing. The main issue is not the staff, but poor management, insufficient capacity, and a lack of personnel for the number of customers they are trying to serve.

For Santa Monica prices, this felt like a real bargain. Hot, tasty, filling, and fast. The crew was cool and professional, and the food came out exactly how you want it — fresh and dialed in.

Google review of XUNTOS (5 out of 5, by Alvaro Hoyos, 6 months ago): Spanish food has a nostalgic place in my heart, so I tend to romanticize every Spanish food meal as I go into them and then get woken up post meal. This was not one of those times.

Xuntos has a pintxos and tapas menu that embodies what I love about Spanish food; the sharing aspect and the ability to experience many more dishes than at other cuisine types (yes, dim sum is up there too). We had 12 or so distinct dishes and the highlights were the croquetas, the anchovies on toast, and the scallops. The lowllights, or meh-lights, were the deviled eggs and the tomato toast; one could have used more flavor (yolk mixture needed more punch) and the other was on the saltier side (and I love salt). Shout-out to the basque whiskey which I don't think I had ever had before and the complimentary rose they gave us with the scallops.

Service was friendly, but seems like they were stretched thin. Either way, it was good and the comp rose was a nice "sorry about the delays". They were accommodating to our patatas bravas with the sauce on the side (french fries for the kids win) and we felt welcomed.

Atmosphere was good, if a bit loud, but I liked the decor, including the scallop shell wall and the various paintings.

Overall, we had a great experience at Xuntos and it is exactly what I imagine when I think of a Spanish meal. Looking forward to the next one.

Google review of CVS (1 out of 5, by Spencer Greenberg, 7 months ago): The pharmacy at this location is consistently unreliable and unprofessional. I have been coming here for over five years—primarily because it is close to where I live—but the level of service has deteriorated significantly.

Constant staff turnover, and the new pharmacy manager is by far the most concerning change. She is rude, dismissive, and unnecessarily combative in every interaction.

Instead of helping resolve issues, she has hung up mid-conversation and suggested I be willing to accept only 10% of my prescribed medication and that I “be happy with that”.

Then shortly after I was issued another notification on the app saying it would be 4 weeks, obviously I called again where I was told they can provide only 10 of the 120 tablets prescribed, or “try again next month.”

All the other reviews pointing out how packed the class is are correct.
Sweat Yoga needs to change that. Especially in a hot room, you want enough space to move your body freely. They maximize profit by squeezing as many people as possible into a hot, sweaty, medium-sized room. I've tried CorePower Yoga (both locations, on 2nd Street and Wilshire), and their classes are much less crowded.

The instructor, Isabel Galler, was excellent; she knew what she was doing and how to keep us motivated and focused. She guided us with her voice soft but firm voice. Are you in good shape? Hot Yoga will humble you really quickly! I had to leave the room for a minute about three times to catch a breath and cool my body a bit.
At the end of the flow, you get a cold, wet, small towel to help your body cool down and recover. I definitely felt rejuvenated after the session.

The women's bathrooms and showers can get crowded. There are lockers in the women's restroom with a lock and code.
The customer service at the front desk could be better. As I walked in, I wasn't greeted in any way.
Street metered parking: If you come to the 6:30 AM class, you will find parking quickly and can put money in the meter at 8 AM so that parking will be free.

docs.text:
Google review of Piper Preschool - Santa Monica (5 out of 5, by J C, in the last week): We absolutely love Piper. From the moment we walked through the doors on my tour, we could feel how much thought, care and love had gone into creating such a special place. My husband was kind of checked out on all of our preschool tours until this one. He was locked in on Piper.

It feels welcoming, sweet, and thoughtful in ways where it feel less like a traditional school and more like a second home. We were worried about all the craziness with schools in this area, but Piper put all of that to rest. From the materials, to the classrooms, to the playground, to all the little learning centers, every detail feels intentional.

The teachers are truly what make Piper so special. Not only are they amazing, kind, patient and nurturing, but they act like they love their job and that makes all the difference. Our kids absolutely love going to school, and as parents, there's no better feeling than seeing your children excited to walk through the doors each morning. Knowing they're surrounded by people who care about them, encourage their curiosity and celebrate their individual personalities gives us so much peace of mind. I really can't say enough good things about Piper. It just feels really right in there.

One of our kids' favorite things about Piper is the creek. It's such a unique and magical feature that we didn't find at any other preschools. Watching the kids explore, play, get their hands dirty and discover the world around them is exactly what childhood should look like. Between the creek, gardens and art spaces, this school creates an outdoor environment where learning feels natural. The kids get to be kids while gaining confidence, independence, creativity and a love of learning.

We're going on our second year and we couldn't be happier. It's the kind of place that makes you appreciate how important these early years are and how much of a difference the right environment and the right people can make. Our kids are happy, excited to learn and surrounded by teachers who make them feel loved and supported. Piper has created something truly special, and we're so grateful to be part of it.

docs.text:
Google review of Palms & Paws Veterinary Center (5 out of 5, by Haley Cohen, 5 months ago): I’ve been bringing my dog to Palms & Paws since 2023. Their consistency and quality of care keeps me coming back for nail trims, annual exams, vaccines, complex concerns, and surgical procedures. Dr. McKevilly is thoughtful, thorough, and genuinely invested in my dog’s long-term health, and provides individualized food, treat, and/or treatment recommendations based on my dog's life stage, activity level, symptoms, and occasional hunger strike.

My dog can be selectively reactive, and Dr. McKevilly consistently prioritizes his comfort by adjusting how and where procedures are done (e.g., in a private patient room and with me present, rather than main exam room in the back), and even rescheduling rather than pushing through high-stress appointments. Palms & Paws' level of awareness, patience, and flexibility with anxious dogs really sets them apart.

At Palms & Paws I've always felt fully informed, genuinely supported to choose what feels best as the owner, and never pressured into decisions. A recent example of this: in March 2026, while my dog was receiving his first dental cleaning, Dr. McKevilly personally called me mid-procedure to evaluate whether to remove his rear dewclaws at the same time (something we've discussed regularly since 2023 and extensively assessed in the weeks leading to the dental cleaning). After walking through the additional procedure step-by-step and weighing all the pros/cons of such, we determined the safest and most efficient option would be to proceed with the dewclaw removal during the dental cleaning, ultimately avoiding a second procedure with anesthesia later on or under emergency circumstances. Recovery was smooth, and the level of follow-up during healing was incredible.

Palms & Paws' follow-up care is excellent, I often hear from Dr. McKevilly the same or next day after visits, and they stay engaged daily during more complex recoveries. Highly recommend Dr. McKevilly at Palms & Paws for anyone looking for a vet who is communicative, patient, and truly cares about both the pet and the owner. I will continue to recommend Palms & Paws to family members, friends, and colleagues with different pets and will trust them with any animal I have in the future.

Google review of Barnes & Noble (5 out of 5, by Aaron Linsdau Thriller Author, 6 months ago): As the author of The Grant Colson Thriller Series and The SERA Archives Thriller Series, I always enjoy visiting bookstores while traveling, and Barnes & Noble is a great addition to the Santa Monica Promenade.

The store feels almost brand new and fits perfectly into the lively pedestrian shopping area along 3rd Street Promenade. The design is very clever. At first the space looks fairly compact, but there is both an upstairs and downstairs level which makes the store feel much larger once you start exploring.

When I visited, there was even a table of puzzles set up near the landing downstairs, which added a fun and welcoming touch to the space.

The layout makes excellent use of the footprint with a strong book selection and comfortable browsing areas throughout the store. While moving through the store, I ended up browsing the romance shelves as well while writing The Maui Desire Romance Series, and it’s a well-organized section that fits naturally into the layout.

The location itself is fantastic, right in the middle of the walking promenade with lots of activity and energy around it.

Parking is also relatively easy thanks to nearby parking garages, which makes visiting the promenade much simpler.

Overall it’s a beautiful new Barnes & Noble location and a great place to browse books while spending time in Santa Monica.

Google review of Barnes & Noble (5 out of 5, by Guillaume Bourcy, a year ago): My family and I treasure our visits to bookshops, especially for finding new books, birthday presents or simply browse their alleys seeking for classics. In Santa Monica, Barnes & Noble has become our preferred destination, especially given the scarce number of bookstores in downtown nowadays. The Barnes & Noble location on 3rd Street Promenade is a delightful addition and stands out as a phenomenal success.

Though it is somewhat smaller than their typical stores, this quality actually enhances its charm, making it feel more authentic and welcoming.

The layout, with two floors, thoughtfully caters to diverse interests. The lower level is wonderfully suited for younger readers, featuring a selection of toys and an impressive, well-curated collection of Mangas that we particularly enjoy. Despite its more compact size, the store does not compromise on variety, offering an extensive range of books across different genres.

What truly sets this location apart, however, is the staff. They are incredibly helpful and friendly, contributing to a sense of customer intimacy that is sometimes lost in larger spaces. It's clear that the cozy atmosphere of this smaller space fosters a closer connection between the staff and patrons.

In summary, our family's experiences at the Barnes & Noble on 3rd Street Promenade have been nothing short of wonderful. It's a gem of a bookstore that we'll continue to visit and support.

Google review of Barnes & Noble (5 out of 5, by Carol, 2 years ago): Went to the grand opening today of the Barns and Noble in Santa Monica, California.
They had a ribbon cutting ceremony. The mayor of Santa Monica spoke, the district manager of this region went around and thanked and welcomed customers for coming.
They have two floors. Areas are compact, nearly organized and the displays are easily accessible.
Lower level has music, games, history, science etc..
Will definitely patronize regularly. There is also a coffee shop right next door.

Google review of Barnes & Noble (2 out of 5, by anapat, 4 months ago): I find befuddling to have recently walked into a couple of Barnes and Nobles (Santa Monica and The Grove) and notice dozens of books on witchcraft and demons prominently displayed but had to ask an employee for the Bible section because I couldn't find it. Upon walking by some more shelves lined with books about spells and what not, at the basement and at the back, there is a little treasure trove hidden from view for only a few who bother to look for it,  inconspicuous and (perhaps) almost purposefully hidden, I find a few Bibles.

I couldn't help bringing it up to a sales associate who told me that while people pick up and browse the witchcraft books, they put them back on the shelf and told me (to my glad surprise) that Bibles actually sell better.

But then I wonder, if they sell better, should they not be displayed more prominently? Go figure.

For years I resisted buying books online to support the physical store. Even if I have to pay a little more, plus the cost of parking, I figured I was doing my part to keep them alive. Several times I drove to Barnes and Noble to pay more for a book that was cheaper on Amazon and would have been delivered to my doorstep at no charge, solely out of principle.

But seeing the kinds of books that they shove on your face while hiding what I find truly edifying and uplifting has turned me off about supporting them. But that's just me.
